title: Determinants
key_idea: The **Lindström–Gessel–Viennot (LGV) lemma**: for a directed acyclic graph with sources $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ and sinks $B_1, \ldots, B_n$, the determinant $\det[e(A_i, B_j)]$ (where $e(u,v)$ = sum of weights of paths $u \to v$) equals the signed sum over $n$-tuples of vertex-disjoint paths. This gives determinantal formulas for many combinatorial quantities (binomial, ballot, Catalan, plane partitions).
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** The LGV lemma is one of the most powerful tools in enumerative combinatorics — a clean determinantal formula arising from a sign-reversing involution on intersecting path systems.
